name: Zimbabwe
summary: Seven horizontal stripes of green, yellow, red and black, with a white triangle at the hoist bearing a red star and the golden Zimbabwe Bird. Adopted at independence in 1980.
origin: The colours come from the flag of the Zimbabwe African National Union – Patriotic Front (ZANU–PF), which led the country to independence from Rhodesia.
The flag was first raised at midnight on 18 April 1980, Independence Day.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood shed in the liberation war.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The heritage and ethnicity of the Black majority.

symbols.name: Zimbabwe Bird
symbols.description: A golden stylised bird in the triangle.
symbols.meaning: The history of the country; carved soapstone birds were found at the ruins of Great Zimbabwe.

symbols.name: Red star
symbols.description: A five-pointed red star behind the bird.
symbols.meaning: The nation's hopes and aspirations; also socialism.

facts: Several of the Great Zimbabwe birds were removed to South Africa and Germany in the colonial era; most have been returned.
Its white triangle points into the stripes like an arrow.
Zambia's flag has a similar palette with a fish eagle.
clues: Green, yellow, red and black stripes with a white triangle holding a bird and a red star.
Its bird was carved in soapstone at a medieval ruined city.
